correctness.rationale: The transpose orbit model is a genuine PL homeomorphism of fixed realizations. Incidence-star minimal nonfaces yield a simplex-boundary nerve for the integral Alexander dual; the resulting homology is a single Z in degree C(n,2)-1. Simple connectivity for n=3 is proved with explicit triangle fans, n>=4 has full 2-skeleton, n=2 is two components; Hurewicz and homology Whitehead prove homotopy spheres. The full-group integral orientation uses natural equivariant Alexander duality with explicit ambient and join signs; exhaustive independent signed Lefschetz and finite mod-two Betti checks agree at n=2,3,4.

originality.rationale: Singh proves the ordinary sphere, and Reiner–Roberts predetermines the side-preserving rational module; these are acknowledged as prior coverage. The novel claim is an all-n fixed-point homotopy sphere for every part-exchanging involution, with a full graph-group orientation extension and quotient dichotomy. Relevant primary comparison sections and indexed research searches found no implication supplying the fixed sphere dimension; this is qualified by unindexed-work risk.
residual_risks: A differently named or unindexed prior fixed-point classification might exist.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a natural complete quadratic-dimension fixed-sphere classification for an infinite family of higher matching homotopy spheres, an invariant not determined by a known nonequivariant sphere or subgroup representation. It adds the full integral bipartition-swapping orientation and a mod-four homological distinction between full symmetry quotients, while explicitly separating prior known results from the new fixed-point fact.
